# Gon standard packages must preserve packages already provided by Go modules.
env GOWORK=off
cd local
go run .
stdout '^\[2 4 6\] local$'
go list -f '{{.Standard}} {{if .Module}}{{.Module.Path}}{{end}}' gon/seq
stdout '^false gon$'
go mod tidy
go test ./...

# Dependencies and vendor mode preserve the same provider and module metadata.
cd ../consumer
go run .
stdout '^\[2 4 6\] local$'
go list -f '{{.Standard}} {{.Module.Path}} {{.Module.Replace.Path}}' gon/seq
stdout '^false gon ../local$'
go mod vendor
go run -mod=vendor .
stdout '^\[2 4 6\] local$'
go list -mod=vendor -f '{{.Standard}} {{.Module.Path}}' gon/seq
stdout '^false gon$'

# A module with no package at that import path still uses Gon's standard package.
cd ../fallback
go run .
stdout '^\[2 4 6\]$'
go list -f '{{.Standard}} {{if .Module}}{{.Module.Path}}{{end}}' gon/seq
stdout '^true $'

# Workspace providers retain their normal module identity.
cd ..
go work init local workspace
env GOWORK=$WORK/gopath/src/go.work
cd workspace
go run .
stdout '^\[2 4 6\] local$'
env GOWORK=off

# Multiple module providers remain ambiguous, rather than arbitrarily choosing.
cd ../ambiguous
! go list gon/seq
stderr 'ambiguous import: found package gon/seq in multiple modules:'
stderr 'gon v0.0.0'
stderr 'gon/seq v0.0.0'
! stderr 'GOROOT'

# GOPATH packages also retain the behavior that predates Gon standard packages.
env GO111MODULE=off
env GOPATH=$WORK/gopath
cd $GOPATH/src/example
go run .
stdout '^\[2 4 6\] local$'
go list -f '{{.Standard}}' gon/seq
stdout '^false$'

-- local/go.mod --
module gon
go 1.27
-- local/seq/seq.go --
package seq
func Map[T, U any](values []T, f func(T) U) []U {
	result := make([]U, len(values))
	for i, value := range values { result[i] = f(value) }
	return result
}
func Origin() string { return "local" }
-- local/main.go --
package main
import "fmt"
import "gon/seq"
func main() { fmt.Println(seq.Map([]int{1, 2, 3}, func(n int) int { return n*2 }), seq.Origin()) }
-- consumer/go.mod --
module example.com/consumer
go 1.27
require gon v0.0.0
replace gon => ../local
-- consumer/main.go --
package main
import "fmt"
import "gon/seq"
func main() { fmt.Println(seq.Map([]int{1, 2, 3}, func(n int) int { return n*2 }), seq.Origin()) }
-- fallback/go.mod --
module gon
go 1.27
-- fallback/main.go --
package main
import "fmt"
import "gon/seq"
func main() { fmt.Println(seq.Map([]int{1, 2, 3}, func(n int) int { return n*2 })) }
-- workspace/go.mod --
module example.com/workspace
go 1.27
-- workspace/main.go --
package main
import "fmt"
import "gon/seq"
func main() { fmt.Println(seq.Map([]int{1, 2, 3}, func(n int) int { return n*2 }), seq.Origin()) }
-- ambiguous/go.mod --
module example.com/ambiguous
go 1.27
require (
	gon v0.0.0
	gon/seq v0.0.0
)
replace gon => ../local
replace gon/seq => ../leaf
-- leaf/go.mod --
module gon/seq
go 1.27
-- leaf/seq.go --
package seq
func Origin() string { return "leaf" }
-- $WORK/gopath/src/gon/seq/seq.go --
package seq
func Map[T, U any](values []T, f func(T) U) []U {
	result := make([]U, len(values))
	for i, value := range values { result[i] = f(value) }
	return result
}
func Origin() string { return "local" }
-- $WORK/gopath/src/example/main.go --
package main
import "fmt"
import "gon/seq"
func main() { fmt.Println(seq.Map([]int{1, 2, 3}, func(n int) int { return n*2 }), seq.Origin()) }
